other_up.note:
A tree with $L$ leaves has some leaf at depth $\le \log_2 L$. The path to a
leaf fixes the input on those coordinates and already determines the output,
so it *is* a certificate for every input reaching it -- and $\mathrm{C}_{\min}$
only asks for one input with a short certificate. Note this needs the $\min$:
the deepest leaf says nothing, which is exactly why $\mathrm{C}$ itself is
**not** bounded by $\log \mathrm{DTsize}$.

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\mathrm{C}_{\min}(f) \le \log_2 \mathrm{DTsize}(f)\)
    putative
    A tree with $L$ leaves has some leaf at depth $\le \log_2 L$. The path to a leaf fixes the input on those coordinates and already determines the output, so it is a certificate for every input reaching it -- and $\mathrm{C}_{\min}$ only asks for one input with a short certificate. Note this needs the $\min$: the deepest leaf says nothing, which is exactly why $\mathrm{C}$ itself is not bounded by $\log \mathrm{DTsize}$.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{C}_{\min}(\oplus_n) = n = \log_2 \mathrm{DTsize}(\oplus_n)\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\)
    Every input of $\oplus_n$ needs all $n$ bits, and its minimal tree is the full binary tree on $2^n$ leaves. Equality, so nothing can be shaved.

This is the $\mathrm{C}_{\min}$ shadow of $\mathrm{rank}\le\log_2\mathrm{DTsize}$ above, and can also be obtained by composing that record with $\mathrm{C}_{\min}\le\mathrm{rank}$ -- but the closure does not chain a polynomial bound through a logarithmic one, so it is recorded directly. Recorded under partial since nothing in the argument uses totality; the total row inherits it. It does not extend to relations, where $\mathrm{C}_{\min}$ is not defined.

see also: \(\mathrm{C}_{\min}(f)\), \(\mathrm{DTsize}(f)\), \(\mathrm{rank}(f)\), \(\mathrm{UC}_{\min}(f)\), \(\oplus_n\) data/relations/10-new-measures.yaml

relation Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every relation

  • \(\mathrm{C}_{\min}(f) \le \mathrm{C}(f)\)
    $\min_x \mathrm{C}_x(f) \le \max_x \mathrm{C}_x(f)$ over a non-empty domain. Nothing here reads the output, so certificates for a search problem -- assignments that fix some valid answer -- behave the same way.

The gap between the two can be everything: $\mathrm{C}_{\min}(\mathrm{OR}_n) = 1$ (any $1$-input has a one-bit certificate) while $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OR}_n) = n$.

see also: \(\mathrm{C}_{\min}(f)\), \(\mathrm{C}(f)\), \(\mathrm{C}^1(f)\) data/relations/13-definitional.yaml
